summary: Iteration 3: focused testing of the new phone-photo upload + hero-video replacement feature (Emergent object storage + chunked uploads) plus a light regression pass. Backend: 35/35 pytest tests pass (new /app/backend/tests/test_uploads.py and test_uploads_db.py cover single-chunk upload, 2-chunk assembly byte-equality, auth, content-type and size limits, 404 on unknown path, site-images validation/merge, db.files record). Frontend: admin login, all 12 media slots (1 video + 11 images), founder photo upload -> /api/files path in slot input + success toast + preview render, hero video upload, save, /founder and Home hero picking up uploaded URLs, reset-to-original + save, RFQ submit, all 8 pages render with no console errors and no broken images at 1920x1080 and 390x844. No blocking issues found.

minor.issue: Size limit is only enforced after all chunks are assembled, and there is no cap on `total` or per-chunk size, so an authenticated admin can write unbounded data into /tmp/fs_uploads before the 400 is returned. Also no cleanup of abandoned partial upload folders in /tmp/fs_uploads.

content_type is taken from the client form field and trusted (no magic-byte sniffing); a text/html payload labelled image/png would be stored and later served with an image content-type. Low risk since serve_file forces the stored content_type, but worth noting.

App sets Cache-Control public,max-age=86400 but the preview ingress rewrites it to no-store, so uploaded media is re-fetched from object storage on every request in preview (informational, not an app bug).
>80MB video rejection was not exercised end-to-end (only the shared limit branch via a 15MB+ image, which returned 400 as expected). Code path reviewed and is identical.

action_items: Optional hardening: validate `total`/chunk size and reject oversize uploads before assembling in /tmp; add a janitor for stale /tmp/fs_uploads folders.
critical_code_review_comments: uploads/chunk writes every chunk to disk before checking the size limit — enforce a running byte budget per upload_id.
Consider sniffing file magic bytes instead of trusting the client-provided content_type form field.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Upload feature verified end-to-end via UI and API. Reusable suites: tests/test_uploads.py (upload/limits/security/site-images), tests/test_uploads_db.py (db.files record + soft-delete 404). Playwright pattern that works for uploads: page.locator('[data-testid="admin-upload-<key>"] input[type=file]').set_input_files({name,mimeType,buffer}); wait ~4s then read the slot input value. Headless Chromium cannot decode H.264 — only assert hero-video src. Always soft-delete TEST_ db.files rows and reset site_config images after testing.
rca_of_the_issue: No functional defects found this iteration. The single pre-existing pytest failure (test_db_persistence) was a stale test asserting on a hardcoded enquiry document from iteration 2, not an application bug; rewritten to be self-contained.
